findings.problem: The bare prompt 'to worry' most naturally means the intransitive 'I worry', which Spanish says with preocuparse, so a fluent speaker could equally answer preocuparse, and nothing rules it out.
findings.fix: hint: to make someone worry, as in 'it worries me' (to worry yourself is preocuparse)

findings.problem: The sentence uses the reflexive preocuparse ('no te preocupes'), not preocupar in its transitive meaning of worrying someone.
findings.fix: example.es: Me preocupa tu salud. / example.en: Your health worries me.

back.es: to worry (someone), to concern; the intransitive 'to worry, be worried' is preocuparse
back.example: Don't worry, everything is going to be fine.

note: You could instead make the card preocuparse (me preocupo, te preocupas, se preocupa) and keep 'No te preocupes'. That fits the prompt 'to worry' and is probably why the word ranks so high in the subtitles list.
